subject: Locale specification (how user and system defaults defined; at least one user and one system default)
notes: (kb/Work PB2671, wave 1040 group S.) cite.py --check A.1 "Locale specification" -> OK §A.1 118); --check 8.2.1 "The implementor shall specify the manner in which the user default locale is defined" -> OK; --check 8.2.1 "The implementor shall specify the manner in which the system default locale is defined and shall provide at least one system default locale" -> OK; --check 14.6.6 "At run unit activation, the user default locale becomes the current locale for the run unit for all locale categories" -> OK 1). A.1-118 need not be documented; §7 documents it voluntarily. The witness asserts a COLLATION ORDER, never a date or number format, so CLDR format drift cannot break it: under ALPHABET ... IS LOCALE with no locale-name (--check 12.3.7.4 "otherwise by the locale that is current" -> OK 7) e)) Spanish sorts nz before ñu and German and the root sort ñu first. Four environments, each run printing the order for the current locale at start, after SET LOCALE LC_ALL TO SYSTEM-DEFAULT and after SET LOCALE LC_ALL TO USER-DEFAULT: COBOL_USER_LOCALE=es-ES COBOL_SYSTEM_LOCALE=de-DE; the two swapped (the orders swap); COBOL_USER_LOCALE=C (the root) with COBOL_SYSTEM_LOCALE=' es_ES.UTF-8 ' (trimmed, POSIX spelling); and neither variable set under DOTNET_SYSTEM_GLOBALIZATION_INVARIANT=1 (both defaults exist, as the root, and the run ends normally). CutRunner.RunExit now removes a variable whose env value is null, which is what reaches the unset arm. The process-culture fallback of the user default is witnessed by the A120 host test (CurrentCulture es-ES at run-unit start makes the user default Spanish).
